title: Employing Three-dimensional Focused-ion Beam Tomography for Comprehensive Mesoscale Characterization of Surface Degradation of Nuclear Materials
content: Three-dimensional (3D) tomography using focused-ion beam (FIB) microscopy has become a powerful technique within the past few years given its ability to generate sub-micron resolution volumes that can expand upon the information acquired two-dimensionally (2D) with scanning electron microscopy (SEM) [1]. This is especially critical for highly contextualized phenomena that need to be captured 3D to get a full perspective on how the material in question has evolved, such as in the case of materials degradation mechanisms (i.e. corrosion, irradiation, etc.) [2-4]. When employed in conjunction with 2D cross-sectional images of the specimen, 3D tomography could expand initial observations, providing highly contextualized information at specific sites of interest identified from 2D analysis, enhancing our contextual information about degradation mechanisms at the mesoscale. Additionally, this 3D information can also provide direct observable data for validating 3D mesoscale modelling for predicting the evolution of microstructure and composition and structural materials. Computational capabilities like these would be especially useful for expediting the qualification of nuclear materials for advanced nuclear reactors [5].
